exp.desc:
- 14 rooms per shift
- Fault reporting, minibars, lost property
- Training new staff

cl.p1: fourteen rooms a shift, each one as if the general manager were checking in: that is how I was trained, and how I have worked for five years. I notice a hair in the basin or a loose curtain rail before the guest does.
cl.p2: I know the routines with laundry, minibars and lost property, report faults to maintenance and train new colleagues. I would like to work in a smaller hotel where people know each other.

cl.p1: for three years I have deputised for our head housekeeper, responsible for twelve staff across four floors. Rotas, room checks, linen orders and coordinating with reception are all part of it.
cl.p2: I would now like to run a department myself. A leisure hotel where departures and arrivals pile up on a Saturday is a new challenge, and peak days like that are exactly what I enjoy organising.

letters.label: Deputy stepping up to head housekeeper
